o1.biggest_strength: It reads the data well and turns the three biggest signals—skip the belt, women lifting it alone, and quiet wheels—into distinct, usable ad ideas in Mokobara’s voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: The suggested cut/scale threshold of about ₹4,500 per concept is too thin to judge purchases reliably, even though the concepts themselves are strong.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the testing rule to a more realistic spend or purchase threshold and add a little more production detail for each format.

o2.biggest_strength: It is highly actionable: it names the winning audiences, handles the scratch/front-pocket risks, gives clear production rules, and chooses the first three concepts for the right data-backed reasons.
o2.biggest_mistake: It occasionally treats typical review lines as direct buyer quotes, so the team should verify exact wording before launch.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace any implied direct testimonials with verified review copy and add one more fresher non-static idea in place of the simpler gift/product frame.

reason: Both are strong and usable tomorrow, but Output 2 is a bit more production-ready and has the better test-read rules. It also puts the under-served women 25 to 40 opportunity first while still covering work flyers and quiet wheels.
